The bleak reading of The Penultimate Truth is also the most testable one. In 2025, most of humanity lives in underground shelters called "ant tanks", where the inhabitants manufacture military robots known as "leadies". They believe that a war between the Wes-Dem and Pac-Peop blocs continues above them, leaving the surface uninhabitable because of combat, radiation, and disease.

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about The Penultimate Truth. Broadcasts from their leader, Talbot Yancy, report destruction and demand continued production. The former enemies' ruling groups maintain the deception while occupying extensive private estates, where they use the robots as servants and guards.

The self that experiences The Penultimate Truth is a committee, not a king. Yancy is a mechanical simulacrum whose speeches are prepared by propagandists called Yance-men. James, president of the Tom Mix tank, faces a crisis when the tank's chief mechanic, Maury Souza, dies of a pancreatic condition.

Reproduction explains more of The Penultimate Truth than any philosophy dares to admit. The tank's physician, Carol Tigh, immediately freezes Souza's body so that he can be revived if an artificial pancreas becomes available. Without Souza, the community risks failing to meet its production quota and being dissolved.

Once you see The Penultimate Truth as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. A committee of residents collects money and pressures Nicholas to seek one on the surface, threatening him with a bomb if he refuses. Nicholas reluctantly agrees and completes a tunnel begun by the committee, expecting to encounter the dangers described in the broadcasts.

The story The Penultimate Truth tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. Above ground, Yance-man Joseph Adams receives an assignment from Brose to help destroy housing developer Louis Runcible. Runcible houses former tank inhabitants in large apartment developments, although the residents remain confined.

Meaning is not found in The Penultimate Truth — it is manufactured for it. Brose suspects him of informing underground communities that the war has ended. Brose plans to plant counterfeit alien weapons and remains beneath Runcible's Utah construction site, using a time-travel device to deposit them centuries in the past.

The cold light on The Penultimate Truth leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. He expects Runcible to conceal their discovery, giving the authorities grounds to imprison him and confiscate his holdings. Adams is assigned to write fraudulent scientific articles establishing the objects' archaeological importance, while his friend Verne Lindblom manufactures the artifacts.

The Penultimate Truth did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. Two leadies capture him, seal his tunnel, and prepare to kill him, but a man resembling Yancy destroys them. Directed toward the ruins of Cheyenne, Nicholas encounters former tank inhabitants who explain that the war has ended and that the broadcasts conceal actual conditions on the surface.

The honest version of The Penultimate Truth starts by giving up the comforting part. Although radioactive areas remain, the world is not the continuous battlefield he expected. Lantano subsequently brings Nicholas to his estate and offers to help him obtain the pancreas.

Strip The Penultimate Truth of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. Brose's scheme is disrupted when his agent at the construction site, Robert Hig, is killed after uncovering a planted artifact. Then Lindblom, who manufactured the counterfeit artifacts, is murdered by a wartime assassination machine that plants false evidence to implicate someone else.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — The Penultimate Truth shows exactly where that breaks. Adams fears that Brose is eliminating those involved in the scheme and seeks protection at Lantano's estate. Investigator Webster Foote examines the clues implicating Brose in Lindblom's murder but recognizes that the machine has fabricated them.

What looks like free choice in The Penultimate Truth is older than choice itself. His investigation also brings him to Lantano's estate, where Nicholas is seeking help obtaining the pancreas. Lantano reveals that he is a Cherokee from the fifteenth century who acquired time-travel technology through the artifacts sent into the past.

Nobody designed the part of The Penultimate Truth you experience — it was inherited. Lantano, Foote, and Adams plan to install a specialized dart weapon in Adams's office, which Brose visits. Privately, Lantano admits to Foote that he killed Hig to protect Runcible and murdered Lindblom to convince Adams that Brose must be eliminated.

Every serious account of The Penultimate Truth eventually collides with the question of who is deciding. Because Brose avoids Lantano, Adams's office provides an opportunity to reach him. With information from Foote and equipment and leadies supplied by Lantano, Nicholas locates a buried medical depot and obtains the pancreas.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of The Penultimate Truth — it is the floor you stand on while examining it.
